clean_apply.method: the generated patch reverse-applies cleanly to the current overlay on the pinned base, proving the overlay bytes are exactly the patch result

initial_failure_before_fix.cause: legacy DWARF address/range/location/aranges writers serialized ELF32 addresses as eight-byte values

dwarf32_contract.policy: the candidate may retain reference verifier findings, but may not introduce a new error class/count, invalid range/location, missing debug section or non-ELF32 aranges width

aarch64_target_scoping.purpose: constant-island, text-data and seven clustered-relaxation controls that failed before ARM-only state was scoped

remaining_failure_classes: the configured clang path names /usr/lib/ccache/clang-18++ for four C++ tests, but that executable does not exist
the configured clang-18 lacks newer AArch64 compare-and-branch, pointer-authentication, CREL and assembler option support used by pinned tests
the configured clang-18 lacks newer RISC-V extensions and assembly behavior used by pinned tests
several profile, DWARF, mapping-symbol, shrink-wrapping and runtime controls remain unresolved against this mixed-version test environment

scope_limits: this milestone establishes ELF32/Cortex-M DWARF address-width preservation and prevents ARM firmware emission state from changing selected AArch64 behavior
the 68-profile matrix and real M4 run are preservation/installation evidence, not complete x86-backend feature parity
the full BOLT lit diagnostic is not clean; 23 failures remain and are recorded rather than suppressed
the M4 FastDyn run checks fixed completed work and exact RAM state, not a statistically powered speedup claim
DWARF verifier findings already present in the reference are retained and named; the gate forbids new findings rather than claiming the input debug information is perfect
patch-aware transformation semantics remain a later phase; this production gate uses the current explicit empty patch contract

source_changes.address_width: legacy and DWARF5 range/location/aranges writers now serialize the owning compile unit's 4- or 8-byte address size instead of assuming eight bytes
source_changes.merge_contract: range/location section mergers use writer-provided terminator widths and reject mixed address sizes that cannot be represented safely
source_changes.target_scoping: instruction-owned data sizing, mapping aliases, data-object handling and thunk origin/accounting are ARM-only; established AArch64 behavior remains on its original path
source_changes.test_contract: the ELF32 smoke test now expects exact Cortex-M CPU qualification because EM_ARM is supported rather than reporting ARM as an unrecognized machine
